 Meesho CEO buys two Bengaluru villa plots from Byju Raveendran's family
 SECTIONS Meesho CEO buys two Bengaluru villa plots from Byju Raveendran's family By Kailash Babar , ET Bureau Last Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 06:26:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Vidit Aatrey, co-founder and CEO of Meesho, acquired two residential villa plots in Bengaluru. The total transaction value for both plots was Rs 83.81 crore, completed through two sale deeds. One plot was purchased from Divya Gokulnath, while the other was acquired from Deeptha Akhila Raghavan. The properties are located in a gated villa community in Yemalur village. Both transactions highlight the ongoing demand for luxury housing in Bengaluru.
 Reuters Meesho co-founder and CEO Vidit Aatrey has purchased two adjoining residential villa plots in Bengaluru from members of Byju Raveendran's family for a combined Rs 83.81 crore.
 Ecommerce platform Meesho ’s co-founder and chief executive Vidit Aatrey has acquired two contiguous residential villa plots in Bengaluru from members of Byju Raveendran 's family for a combined Rs 83.81 crore
 The transactions, executed through two separate sale deeds, involve a combined land area of 33,485 sq ft in a gated villa community, located in Yemalur village , Varthur Hobli, in Bengaluru East. Both transactions were concluded on July 24, and registered on July 27.
In the first transaction, Aatrey purchased an 18,305 sq ft plot from Divya Gokulnath, wife of Byju Raveendran, for Rs 48.11 crore. The second transaction involved a 15,180 sq ft parcel acquired from Deeptha Akhila Raghavan, wife of Riju Raveendran, Byju Raveendran's brother, for Rs 35.70 crore. 
The combined transaction value works out to around Rs 25,029 per sq ft. The two parcels form part of Plot B12 within the residential enclave, showed the registration documents accessed through realty data analytics platform Zapkey.
The sale deeds include detailed indemnification clauses and representations by the sellers, addressing potential legal and financial liabilities. Both sellers have represented that the properties are self-acquired, free of encumbrances and not subject to any attachments or proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) or tax laws.
 Live Events
 These representations assume significance amid ongoing insolvency and legal proceedings involving Think & Learn Pvt Ltd, the parent company of education technology firm BYJU'S. The sale deeds also include warranties concerning the ownership and legal status of the properties.
 ET’s email queries to Meesho and Byju’s teams remained unanswered.
The transactions add to high-value residential property deals in Bengaluru, where demand for large villa plots in established gated communities has remained a key segment of the luxury housing market .
